messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for /v1/generate across prod-hostpool-a. p95 went 300ms -> 1.8s, p99 700ms -> 6.7s in the last 5m. Error rate stable. tag: latency, severity: high
oncall-bot: context: 80% of requests are hitting model rw-xxl-v1, avg seq len 512, batching rate up 2.5x
sam: saw the alert, looking at traces now. queuing/KV cache looks normal. any traffic pattern changes?
elaine: on it. if error rate is stable I suspect a slowdown in the model worker pools or kernel fallback. sam, can you check GPU utilization and kernel time breakdown?
sam: GPU util on prod-hostpool-a jumped to 96% on two nodes, but the rest are 40-60%. scheduling skew? also seeing increased tail latency in `attention` kernels in recent traces. attaching snippet:
```
trace sample: request_id=abc123
kernel timings: attention=4.1ms -> 28.7ms, matmul=1.3ms -> 2.0ms
node: gpux-12
stack: serving-runtime v2.5.1
```
elaine: okay that points to either a bad kernel selection or a model variant with longer sequence path. mike, did any rollout hit prod in last hour?
mike: rolled out a small runtime config change 35m ago to tweak batcher timeout (reduce from 20ms -> 10ms) to improve latency under light load. rollout targeted a subset but might have affected scheduler heuristics. I paused the rollout when I saw the alert.
nisha: customer escalations incoming. two enterprise customers complained about perceived regressions, one reporting 2.5–3s responses on chat flows. they provided repro (single-turn, 400 tokens) — I'll attach.
elaine: mitigation playbook time. Quick wins to reduce p95/p99: 1) enable circuit breaker on route /v1/generate to shed excess traffic (percent-based), 2) route heavy-tail customers to a fallback model with lower per-token latency, 3) increase worker count on the impacted hostpool or redistribute, 4) temporarily widen batch timeout to avoid kernel path regressions, 5) enable prefix caching for repeated prompts. Which we can do right now?
sam: I can enable route-level circuit breaker and carve out 15% of traffic to fallback model rw-medium-quant8 in <2m. also can flip batcher timeout back to 20ms quickly.
mike: I can scale up prod-hostpool-a by spinning 2 hot nodes (will be warm within ~90s).
ops-runbook-bot: RUNBOOK: apply-circuit-breaker --route=/v1/generate --threshold=95 --mode=percent --shed=15 --note="auto-mitigate p99 spike"
sam: running the runbook now. curl to controller:
```
curl -X POST https://controller.internal/api/traffic/actions \
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
 -d '{"action":"apply_circuit_breaker","route":"/v1/generate","shed_pct":15}'
```
ops-runbook-bot: OK: circuit breaker applied, shed 15% to fallback pool `fallback-rw-medium-quant8` (instances: 18).
sam: flipping batcher timeout back to 20ms on affected pools. patch: `batcher.timeout_ms=20`
ops-runbook-bot: OK: batcher config reverted on prod-hostpool-a.
mike: started scale-up of 2 nodes in hostpool-a; expected ready in ~110s.
elaine: good. nisha, tell customers we've applied protective routing and are seeing improvements; share ETA 3–5m for stabilization. keep logs of repros.
nisha: messaging: "We've applied routing protections and a fallback model to reduce tail latency. We're monitoring — ETA 3–5m for visible improvements. Thank you for the repros, they helped." sending now. :phone:
sam: metrics update: p95 dropped from 1.8s -> 600ms within 90s after apply. p99 down from 6.7s -> 1.4s. errors unchanged. looks effective.
elaine: nice. let's capture the root cause while things are stabilizing. hypothesis: batcher timeout change caused more micro-batches hitting a slower kernel path for long sequences — leading to attention kernel thrash under certain model shapes.
sam: I pulled kernel selection logs: the runtime switched to fallback slow attention kernel when seq_len > 384 and batch size > 12. The reduced timeout produced more small batches, but scheduling aligned batches with longer seq that triggered the slow path.
mike: that fits. rollout change had unintended interaction with seq-length distribution. we'll rollback the rollout and add a safety guard: only apply batcher timeout change when seq_len_avg < 200 for a pool.
elaine: action items (short-term):
- sam: keep circuit breaker at 15% until next deploy gating (monitor 30m)
- mike: rollback rollout flag and add seq_len guard in config (PR and patch)
- ops: autoscale policy tweak: allow one immediate hot add for 3 min under p99 spike
- nisha: collect customer repros and confirm fix with them
- ops-runbook-bot: create ticket for postmortem and SLO guardrail updates
sam: acknowledging. leaving the circuit breaker in place but will reduce shed if p99 stays low.
ops-runbook-bot: TICKET CREATED: #SRE-4289 - "p99 regression due to batcher timeout/seq_len interaction" — include traces, kernel logs, customer repros.
elaine: longer-term guardrails we should add to the playbook:
- automatic route-level rate cap for enterprise keys when p95>target and p99 rising (graceful shedding)
- circuit-breaker should support multi-dim policies (by seq_len and api_key)
- fallback model pool warmed and health-checked per region (eu/west/na)
- automated rollback of recent runtime config rollouts if p99 spike detected within 10m of rollout
- alert enrichment with "likely cause" hints (e.g., kernel path changes, rollout tag)
please add to the SLO doc.
mike: will add the automated rollback job. PR incoming today.
sam: note for runbook: when applying fallback routing, ensure token-cost exposure communicated to billing team — fallback to quantized models can change token cost slightly.
elaine: good catch. nisha, coordinate with billing for any customer-facing cost notes.
nisha: noted. pinging billing.
elaine: postmortem checklist: timeline, exact config diff, kernel logs, reproducer, customer impact, mitigation timeline, and guardrail PRs. assign owners.
sam: I'll own reproducer and kernel log extraction.
mike: I'll own rollout guard and autoscale policy tweak.
ops-runbook-bot: Reminder: please add the incident severity and customer impact to the ticket within 24h.
elaine: thanks team. this is a good example of how small runtime heuristics can cascade. once SRE-4289 is triaged we'll update the runbook and SLOs to avoid repeats. :white_check_mark:
